quickSummary: Spring wood (wide vessels, low density, light color) + Autumn wood (narrow vessels, high density, dark color) form one Annual Growth Ring (Dendrochronology). Heartwood (Duramen) is the dark, non-conducting central core blocked by balloon-like parenchymatous Tyloses and impregnated with tannins/resins, providing rot resistance; Sapwood (Alburnum) is the peripheral functional region that conducts water.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Annual Ring = 1 Spring Wood ring + 1 Autumn Wood ring. Heartwood = Dark, dead, blocked by tyloses (no conduction); Sapwood = Light, functional (active conduction).

conceptBreakdown.content: Secondary xylem (**Wood**) reflects seasonal cambial rhythms, physiological aging, and taxonomic lineage.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.1 Spring Wood vs. Autumn Wood (Annual Rings)
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.1 Spring Wood vs. Autumn Wood (Annual Rings)
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Parameter | Spring Wood (Early Wood) | Autumn Wood (Late Wood) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Formation Period** | Formed during spring season when cambium is highly active | Formed during winter/autumn when cambium is less active |
| **Vessel Lumen Size** | **Wide, broad lumens** with thin-walled tracheary elements | **Narrow lumens** with thick-walled tracheary elements |
| **Wood Color & Density** | **Lighter in color**; **lower density** | **Darker in color**; **higher density** |
| **Dendrochronology** | One concentric ring of Spring Wood + one ring of Autumn Wood form a single **Annual Ring** used to estimate tree age. | |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.2 Heartwood (Duramen) vs. Sapwood (Alburnum)
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.2 Heartwood (Duramen) vs. Sapwood (Alburnum)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
WOOD ANATOMICAL REGIONS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  HEARTWOOD (Duramen)                                     SAPWOOD (Alburnum)
 ├── Central older region of stem                        ├── Peripheral younger region of stem
 ├── Non-functional (Does NOT conduct)                   ├── Functional (Active water conduction)
 ├── Impregnated with tannins, resins, oils, & gums      ├── Lighter in color; non-impregnated
 └── Tracheary elements blocked by **Tyloses**           └── Susceptible to fungal decay
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Heartwood (Duramen)**: The central, darker, older secondary xylem. Tracheary elements are permanently occluded by **Tyloses** and filled with preservative aromatic substances (tannins, resins, oils, gums). It is non-functional for sap conduction and provides immense mechanical strength and decay resistance.
• **Sapwood (Alburnum)**: The peripheral, lighter-colored secondary xylem. Actively conducts water and dissolved mineral nutrients from roots to leaves.
• **Tyloses**: Balloon-like bladder outgrowths of adjacent living xylem ray parenchyma cells that protrude into vessel/tracheid lumens through pit cavities, sealing the conduits during heartwood transformation.
